$about: THE CORRECTING-LINE LEDGER. Requirement 4 of the brief asks for a judgement split —
how much of each wrapper is STYLING and how much is CORRECTING upstream — and it asks
for the correcting lines to be identified and listed rather than estimated. This file is
that list, and it is DATA rather than prose so `measure.mjs` can re-validate it: every
`text` below must still occur in its file exactly `occurrences` times, or the harness
aborts. A judgement that silently stops matching the code is worse than no judgement.
Everything NOT listed here is classified mechanically by the harness:
styling   — a line inside a `cva(...)` call, or a line carrying `className`/`cn(`
imports   — an import statement
invariant — a line mentioning `LumoNode` (Lumo's rule 0; it would be written against
ANY library, so counting it as 'correcting React Aria' would overstate
the upstream cost and understate it for the Base UI comparison)
structure — interface/function boilerplate and JSX composition
`kind` vocabulary, chosen so the Base UI phase can compare like with like:
required-prop-shim   a prop re-declared REQUIRED because upstream leaves it optional
and falls back to an English string, or to nothing at all
aria-fix             an attribute written to overwrite or supply an announced string
slot-claim           wiring upstream only performs if the wrapper names the slot
ssr-fix              exists because upstream's FIRST BYTE differs from its hydrated
tree — the useSlot/useSlotId class of defect
rtl-fix              exists because upstream's own output is direction-blind
type-narrowing       a type that makes an upstream-representable wrong value unwritable
upstream-workaround  behaviour re-derived because upstream drops or ignores it
